clue.text: A sham critic could possibly be appealing

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase could possibly be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A fraudulent reviewer might nonetheless come across as charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is personal magnetism, so a person with it is attractive and appealing to others.

clue.text: Difficult keeping old collection stored away?

indicators.note: the word for difficult is keeping, that is holding within it, the abbreviation for old

parts.note: difficult means hard

explanation.surface: A tricky business, holding on to an antique collection kept in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stash of valuables or supplies amassed and hidden away; the question mark marks a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Keeping school punishment with new head taking over

indicators.note: the punishment word is given a different first letter in place of its own

parts.note: detention is being kept in after school as a penalty
R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A school detention handed out as the new headteacher takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking over' reads as a new head teacher arriving, but 'taking' supplies R (Latin recipe, 'take'), which replaces the D at the head of DETENTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the act of holding on to something, a synonym for keeping in the noun sense.

clue.text: Dance when lifting business degree

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word for when reads it upwards, so backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: Someone takes up dancing while earning a business qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian ballroom and carnival dance.

clue.text: Point a major road uphill

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means the road's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Directions telling someone to head up a main road.
explanation.definitionFit: To point a weapon or camera is to aim it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Tough sports event to flatten many, but not all

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them flat

indicators.note: only part of the word many is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A gruelling contest that knocks out many of its entrants, if not every one.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ironman is an endurance triathlon of swimming, cycling and a full marathon run.

clue.text: Swear he misled when covering fight location

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round, covering, the word for fight
the letters of the two words are led astray into a new order

parts.note: a bout is a boxing or wrestling contest

explanation.surface: A man lies under oath to hide where a brawl took place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misled' rearranges SWEAR HE into WHEREAS, and 'covering' puts that round BOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's whereabouts is the place where they are, so it stands for a location.

clue.text: Fail to give full details to brusque coppers?

definitions.text: Fail to give full details to

parts.note: brusque means curt or abrupt in manner
coppers are low-value copper coins, loose coins in a pocket

explanation.surface: Accusing curt police officers of withholding information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but here it means low-value copper coins, so short coins become short change.
explanation.definitionFit: To shortchange is to give back too little money, or more broadly to deprive someone of what they are due.

clue.text: Cordiality and warmth — that's about right

indicators.note: the word for warmth goes about, around, the abbreviation for right

parts.note: heat is warmth

explanation.surface: Someone approves of friendliness and warmth as the proper qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart can mean warmth of feeling and generosity, a near synonym for cordiality.

clue.text: Large insect found behind mother

indicators.note: the insect word is placed behind, after, the word for mother

parts.note: mam is an informal word for mother
a moth is a winged insect

explanation.surface: A big bug turns up at the back of Mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means huge, from the prehistoric elephant.

clue.text: Superfluous, and under changes with time

indicators.note: the two words are changed into another order

explanation.surface: Something no longer needed, revised and timed again.
explanation.definitionFit: Redundant means no longer needed or more than required, a synonym of superfluous.

clue.text: Take vital moves, providing a running commentary?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words move around into a new order

explanation.surface: A commentator calling the crucial moves in a chess match.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatty person who keeps up a constant stream of words is talkative; the question mark flags the playful description.

clue.text: Spoil horse, having tail docked

indicators.note: docking a tail cuts it short, so the horse word loses its last letter

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A horse is ruined by having its tail cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to damage or ruin it, a synonym for spoil.

clue.text: Such as vinegar, excellent applied to nervous condition

indicators.note: the first word is attached to the next, one placed after the other

parts.note: ace means excellent
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Vinegar being recommended as a remedy for nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic means of or like acetic acid, the sour component of vinegar.

clue.text: English trees? Nonsense

parts.note: two kinds of tree: yew and ash

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses English trees as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is humbug or claptrap meant to impress, a synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: In charge after curtailment of prison medical centre

indicators.note: the abbreviation for in charge comes after the shortened prison
curtailing cuts off the tail, the last letter of the prison word

parts.note: the clink is slang for a prison

explanation.surface: A prison medical unit taken over after budget cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a place where outpatients receive medical treatment or advice.

clue.text: Individual working with energy

parts.note: on means operating, as a machine that is on
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lone person keeps working with plenty of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: One means a single individual person, as in 'one never knows'.

clue.text: Lost again at sea, looking back over one's course?

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sailor lost at sea once more, glancing back at the route.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is wistful longing for the past, a looking back over one's life; the question mark marks the cryptic phrasing.

clue.text: Directive for one young man has overlooked name

parts.note: say introduces an example, as in 'take a fruit, say an apple'

indicators.note: the son has missed out, overlooked, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: a son is a young man

explanation.surface: A rule handed to a boy who forgot to put down his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their authorisation or command, a synonym for directive.

clue.text: Men overheard in this pretence

indicators.note: overheard means the word for men is heard said rather than read

parts.note: guys are men

explanation.surface: Men caught gossiping during a charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance concealing the truth, as in 'under the guise of', so a pretence.

clue.text: Attempt to accommodate ancient play like Hamlet

indicators.note: the word for attempt makes room for, takes in, the word for ancient

parts.note: a try is an attempt
aged means very old

explanation.surface: A theatre company attempts to stage an old Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is one of Shakespeare's great tragedies, so it is an example of the genre.

clue.text: Attention seized by the artist

indicators.note: the letters are seized, held inside, the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A painter grabs everyone's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone an ear means listening to them, so the word stands for attention.

clue.text: What's topping individual cakes, including nice gateaux?

definitions.text: What's topping individual cakes, including nice gateaux?

indicators.note: the tops, the first letters, of the five words that follow are taken

explanation.surface: Asking what decorates small cakes and fancy gateaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread on top of cakes.

clue.text: The writer put in revised other term for measuring device

indicators.note: the setter's word for themselves is put into the rearranged letters
the two words are revised into a different order

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: An author inserts a different term into a revised draft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges OTHER TERM into THERMOTER, and 'put in' places ME inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermometer is an instrument for gauging temperature.
